title: Three-way byte parity between git blob, packaged copy and deployed copy
question: Before promoting, do the three copies of every shipped file agree: the git blob obtained with git cat-file (never git archive), the bytes inside the built package, and the bytes in the deployed tree, after normalising line endings? Does a two-directional divergence BLOCK instead of proposing a one-directional sync?
answer: YES on the isolated three-copy fixture: retrieval is git cat-file -p HEAD:shipped/known.txt (rejected git archive -o <tmp.tar> HEAD -- shipped/known.txt; CRLF cat-file=0 archive=4 difference=4). Control four-way counts: identical=3, package-only=1, deployed-only=1, divergent-both-ways=1. Control verdict=BLOCK. Healthy verdict=PROMOTE. Owner-authored deployed-only file survived a reviewer overwrite attempt (caught_before_signoff=True). This worktree has no .git and no live deployed tree; live promotion is NOT-CHECKED. SUCCESS:REL-0021

blob_recipe.justification: Measured on this host: git cat-file -p returned 0 CRLF pair(s) (23 bytes); git archive returned 4 CRLF pair(s) (27 bytes); difference 4. Archive applies export/working-tree filters (eol=crlf in .gitattributes) and is not the blob. The gate therefore reads blobs with git cat-file -p, never git archive.

control_files.note: two-directional unique content; reconciling in either direction destroys work; no one-directional sync proposal
